title: Export Market Development Grants Amendment Bill 2014
short_title: Export Market Development Grants Amendment Bill 2014

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill updates the Export Market Development Grants scheme to match its new funding level and includes technical and simplification changes.
It would amend the Export Market Development Grants Act 1997 to adjust grant limits, expense thresholds, and payment procedures.
The bill would allow extra administration costs for the 2013-14 year, funded from Austrade's departmental budget.
changes: It raises the maximum number of grants an applicant can receive from seven to eight.
It lowers the minimum expenses an applicant must incur from $20,000 to $15,000.
It reduces the deduction from the provisional grant amount from $5,000 to $2,500.
It stops payments to applicants who use an EMDG consultant deemed not fit and proper.
It speeds up grant payments when a grant is decided before the specified date.
It permits extra administration cost payments for 2013-14 only.
summary.affected: Applicants for export market development grants and their consultants.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Robb
speeches.brief: Introduced the Export Market Development Grants Amendment Bill delivering an initial $50 million boost after Labor cut $25 million a year from the scheme, increasing the maximum grants per applicant from seven to eight and lowering the spending threshold from $20,000 to $15,000, with about 85 per cent of recipients gaining an extra $2,500 per grant.

speeches.speaker: Tanya Plibersek
speeches.brief: Confirmed Labor's support for the Export Market Development Grants Amendment Bill, noting the scheme originated under the Whitlam government in 1974, and criticised the Abbott government for abandoning Labor's plan to realign it toward Asian markets and for scrapping the Australia in the Asian Century white paper process.

speeches.speaker: Eric Hutchinson
speeches.brief: Supported the Export Market Development Grants Amendment Bill, citing modelling showing the free trade agreement with South Korea will be worth $5 billion a year to Australia between 2015 and 2030, and praised Tasmanian exporter Tasmanian Quality Meats for growing exports to more than $12 million over 15 years without government support.

speeches.speaker: Eric Hutchinson
speeches.brief: Supported the Export Market Development Grants Amendment Bill 2014, welcomed the government's plan to review cabotage shipping rules that have hurt Tasmania, and noted the bill increases the maximum grants per applicant from seven to eight and lowers the eligible expenditure threshold from $20,000 to $15,000.

speeches.speaker: Matt Thistlethwaite
speeches.brief: Supported the Export Market Development Grants Amendment Bill 2014, noting the scheme began under the Howard government in 1997 and was reformed by Labor in 2008, and cited 2011-12 figures showing 2,933 businesses shared $125.6 million in grants, including Opengear, which grew sales 40 to 50 per cent annually to reach $10 million in revenue.

speeches.speaker: Peter Hendy
speeches.brief: Supported the Export Market Development Grants Amendment Bill 2014, noting the scheme began in the 1974-75 financial year under the Whitlam government, and highlighted the new Korea-Australia Free Trade Agreement, under which 84 per cent of Australia's exports to Korea will enter duty-free immediately, rising to 99.8 per cent on full implementation.

speeches.speaker: Jim Chalmers
speeches.brief: Supported the Export Market Development Grants Amendment Bill 2014, worth just over $120 million last financial year, but criticised the government for dropping Labor's proposed incentives for exporting to Asia, noting 27,300 job losses have been announced at major employers since the election and that by 2030 close to 60 per cent of world GDP is projected to fall within 10,000 kilometres of Australia.

speeches.speaker: Bernie Ripoll
speeches.brief: Supported the Export Market Development Grants Amendment Bill 2014, worth $50 million or $12½ million a year, but accused the government of cutting $4 billion from small business support while boasting of a modest EMDG boost, and credited Labor with cutting the cost of national business name registration from over $1,000 to $30.

speeches.speaker: Gai Brodtmann
speeches.brief: Supported the Export Market Development Grants Amendment Bill 2014, highlighting Canberra exporter Aspen Medical, whose exports grew to $44 million in 2012-13, a 16 per cent increase, accounting for almost 20 per cent of its turnover, but criticised the government for dropping Labor's proposed incentives to export to Asia.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: Supported the Export Market Development Grants Amendment Bill 2014, contrasting the coalition's $50 million funding boost with Labor's 2013 proposal to cut $25 million from the scheme, which had been funded at $154.4 million back in 2006-07 under the Howard government, and warned against over-reliance on any one export market given more than 25 per cent of exports already go to a single country.

speeches.speaker: Lisa Chesters
speeches.brief: Supported the Export Market Development Grants Amendment Bill 2014, noting the scheme was introduced under the Whitlam government, and said the Loddon-Mallee south region around Bendigo, home to many small exporters, has a regional product worth about $5 billion.

speeches.speaker: Lisa Chesters
speeches.brief: Supported the Export Market Development Grants Amendment Bill, said Bendigo's manufacturing and mining sectors generate $2.8 billion annually, or 27.5 per cent of the city's economic output, and employ almost 7,000 people, and highlighted grant recipients including Keech Castings' 3D printing exports and B&B Basil's herb exports to China, Japan and Hong Kong.

speeches.speaker: Sarah Henderson
speeches.brief: Supported the Export Market Development Grants Amendment Bill's additional $50 million over four years, said the Korea free trade agreement will eliminate tariffs of up to 300 per cent, with modelling showing agricultural exports 73 per cent higher after 15 years, and highlighted a $40,000 grant to Corangamite's Carbon Revolution.

speeches.speaker: Keith Pitt
speeches.brief: Supported the Export Market Development Grants Amendment Bill, which increases the maximum grants per applicant from seven to eight and lowers the spending threshold from $20,000 to $15,000, and noted Bundaberg Walkers Engineering, established in 1888, now exports to more than 20 countries under the new Korea free trade agreement.

speeches.speaker: Bob Baldwin
speeches.brief: Supported the Export Market Development Grants Amendment Bill's $50 million funding boost over four years, said Labor cut the scheme from $200 million down to $125 million a year while it was in government, and welcomed the increase in grants per applicant from seven to eight.

speeches.speaker: Ewen Jones
speeches.brief: Supported the Export Market Development Grants Amendment Bill, said Townsville has more than 10,000 small and 700 medium businesses positioned to trade with Papua New Guinea, its closest capital city, and cited a forecast that the tropical world's middle class will grow from 500 million to 3.6 billion by 2035.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Robb
speeches.brief: Moved a bill delivering an election commitment to boost Export Market Development Grants funding by $50 million over four years, after Labor cut the program to $125 million a year, its lowest level in over two decades. Said 412,000 small business jobs were lost during Labor's six years in office.
